Just throwing some stuff out to get it off my chest. All the little things I've been thinking about recently, so if anyone wants to pop in for a discussion, that's cool too.

Fair warning, most of this shit is gonna be disjointed because I'm just writing it as I think it.

Politics

They say don't talk about politics with family, friends or someone you just started dating. Why? I think it's bullshit. I think politics is the most important thing to discuss and should be got out of the way as soon as possible.

Your political views are a direct reflection of your moral compass. You can learn a lot about how a person treats others (and will treat you) by their politics. I think it's best to get that shit out of the way as soon as humanly possible.

For me, I like to ask people "What's more important? Liberty or equality?" From there, discuss the response. You can learn a lot by how hesitant (or not) they are to answer the question.

I have yet to really get along with anyone that answers with 'equality,' simply because they can't define it when asked. Is everyone equally broke? Equally rich? I'm only 5'9", can I join the NBA? There's a little boy with cerebral palsy who loves the NFL, can he be made quarterback? What about people like Fallon Fox, how's he doing these days?

Life Ain't Fair

A person's attitude to this universal statement can (in classic /b/tard wisdom) "expose their power level."

Nobody wishes life would be fair when good things are happening to them. You don't win the lottery and run up and down the block yelling "FUCK! I WISH LIFE WAS FAIR!" But you'll hear it plenty when someone's car gets broken into, they get passed over for that promotion or that girl turns them down.

You don't wish life was fair, asshole. You wish life was unfair in your favor.

The fact that life is unfair means you have just as much of a shot at getting what you want as anyone else. Oh boohoo, so Drumpf was born with a silver spoon, got a small loan of a million bucks. Ask the average person that wants life to be fair what they'd do with a million bucks -- no, not a loan, a literal windfall. You'll hear shit like "buy a lambo," "pay off my credit cards lol," "buy my parents that house they always wanted." In other words, they'd do all the things they'd normally do on a more extravagant level -- the same shit that keeps them where they are.

"Let's Keep Politics Out of It"

Or alternatively, "let's not get political." You often hear it as a response to something else, not a precursor to discussion. This basically translates to "I have my views and I'm not gonna change them for shit so don't say anything that might make me question my beliefs." It's akin to some fat fuck saying "let's not talk nutrition" after asking you what you think of their beetus or some shit, I don't know, metaphors are hard.

Celebrities need to shut the fuck up.

Not all of them. Just most. There are some out there, rare as they may be, that know how incredibly fortunate they are to have it all -- good looks, health, money, fame, whatever. The problem is the vast majority have all this shit and think their role in life is to improve the world. They have all of the influence and none of the expertise.

After the Parkland shooting, people started pointing out soyboy Hogg and how just being involved in some sort of gun-related incident doesn't confer expertise. The reality is this sort of thing has been going on for way longer. People like Alyssa Milano are among the worst examples.

Politicians are as disconnected from reality as you can get, they're essentially on the same wavelength as the celebrities I described except with policy-making power. You think a politician really gives a fuck if you get to own a bump stock or higher minimum wage or school choice? No matter what happens, at the end of the day they return to a lifestyle most will never experience. They're in mansions surrounded by armed security enjoying a fat salary, and while there's nothing wrong with that in of itself, the ones that proclaim they're "one of us" or try to play off like they're just an everyday person like you or me is delusional at best and downright deceptive at worse.

Good ideas don't need to be defended.

If someone you're talking to (whether romantically or otherwise) says anything along the lines of "I don't like talking politics," what they're really saying is "my ideas have no factual basis that I'm aware of, so don't question them."

Good ideas can be torn apart, examined and put back together without losing integrity. You should want people to question your ideas, that's how they get better. You know your idea is the best it can be when you can no longer find faults, and that's why discourse is so valuable. But no, idiots will say some shit like "everyone deserves a living wage" or "medicare for all" and then in the same breath say "but I don't like to talk politics!"
